- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, particularly if recent prices are trending down; adjust downward bias.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive over last 5–7 days, reduce forecast slope downward to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day of sentiment decay.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong reversal (e.g., >2 consecutive negative sentiment values).
